themes_detail.label: E-Scooter Surge in Throgs Neck
themes_detail.summary: E-scooter complaints spiked to 4 complaints THIS WEEK compared to a 0.6 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 540% spike (z-score: 4.85)—suggesting either a new rental deployment, user behavior change, or emerging safety/obstruction issues in the district.
evidence: 4 e-scooter complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average (540% increase, z-score: 4.85)
Represents a statistically significant anomaly with high severity classification
No prior pattern of e-scooter complaints in baseline data suggests new phenomenon
reporting_angles: Did a dockless scooter operator (Lime, Bird, Citi Scooter) recently launch service in CD 210? Interview operators and DOT.
Talk to residents about safety and obstruction complaints; are scooters blocking sidewalks or creating hazards on narrow Throgs Neck streets?

themes_detail.label: Disposal Crisis in Co-op City
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints exploded to 12 last week versus a 1.4 weekly baseline over 8 weeks—a 773% spike (z-score: 8.72, highest severity)—indicating a possible sanitation contract disruption, bulky item pickup failure, or illegal dumping surge in the district.
evidence: 12 residential disposal complaints last week vs. 1.4 weekly average (773% increase, z-score: 8.72—the highest z-score in dataset)
Classified as 'high severity' anomaly, indicating sustained or worsening condition
Aligns with repeated CB budget requests for 'Other capital budget request for DEP,' suggesting long-standing infrastructure concerns
reporting_angles: Check with DSNY: did the sanitation contract for CD 210 change, or was there a service disruption (truck breakdown, route cancellation)?
Visit Co-op City and Throgs Neck to document any visible dumping or overflowing bins; interview residents about collection delays or missed pickups.

themes_detail.label: Construction & Plumbing Surge
themes_detail.summary: General construction and plumbing complaints jumped to 17 last week from a 4.1 weekly average—a 312% spike (z-score: 5.56)—correlating with a surge in DOB permits (304 filed in last 90 days, with 213 alteration filings) and suggesting accelerated renovation activity or poor contractor oversight.
evidence: 17 construction/plumbing complaints last week vs. 4.1 weekly average (312% increase, z-score: 5.56)
304 DOB permits filed in last 90 days: 213 alteration filings, 48 new buildings, 9 demolitions—indicating sustained construction activity
Spike in complaints coincides with active ULURP rezonings (815 Hutchinson River Parkway in review phase; Bruckner Sites, Bally's Ferry Point recently completed)
reporting_angles: Profile a few of the 213 active alteration projects: are contractors operating without proper permits, creating noise after hours, or damaging shared infrastructure?
Interview DOB and CB about enforcement: are violations being cited and remedied, or are complaints piling up?

themes_detail.label: Tree Damage & Environmental Stress
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage and dead/dying tree complaints combined (3 illegal damage last week + 4 dead/dying trees 2 weeks ago) show a 1100% and 967% spike respectively, suggesting either environmental stress from recent weather, contractor negligence, or a lack of tree care maintenance in the district.
evidence: 3 illegal tree damage complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% increase, z-score: 6.35)
4 dead/dying tree complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (967% increase, z-score: 5.21)
Correlates with high construction activity (304 DOB permits) and recent spike in illegal tree damage tied to construction sites
reporting_angles: Walk neighborhoods and photograph dead or damaged trees; connect to construction sites nearby to establish causation.
Interview Parks Dept about tree maintenance schedules and contractor penalties for tree damage in CD 210; are violations being enforced?

themes_detail.label: Noise Complaints Double
themes_detail.summary: Residential noise complaints surged to 20 last week from a 6.1 weekly baseline—a 226% spike (z-score: 6.84)—likely driven by the construction surge and unregulated construction hours, warranting investigation into evening/weekend violations.
evidence: 20 noise complaints last week vs. 6.1 weekly average (226% increase, z-score: 6.84)
Spike closely tracks construction/plumbing surge (312% increase same timeframe), suggesting construction noise as primary driver
Noise (residential) ranked 5th among top 10 complaint categories over 90 days (713 total complaints)
reporting_angles: Sample a few noise complaints and geolocate them to active construction sites; determine if contractors are working outside permitted hours.
Interview residents on quiet blocks about whether recent construction spikes have disrupted sleep or quality of life.
